reason: The Neumann conclusion silently requires Y (equivalently the operator algebra B(Y)) to be complete, but neither node 1.2 nor 1.2.2 assumes this. Concrete counterexample: let Y=X=c_00 with the l1 norm, J=I, let S be the right shift, T=-(1/4)S, and A=I+T. Then ||J^{-1}||=1, ||A-J||=||T||=1/4, and ||T||<=1/3, yet I_Y+T=I-(1/4)S is not surjective: a preimage of e_1 would have to be (1,1/4,1/16,...) which is not in c_00. Thus the partial Neumann sums are Cauchy only in the completion and do not converge in Y, so the asserted two-sided inverse does not exist without a Banach/completeness premise.
